import { NextResponse } from "next/server";
import type { NextRequest } from "next/server";
import formidable from "formidable";
import fs from "fs";
import path from "path";
import pdf from "pdf-parse";
import mammoth from "mammoth";
import { supabaseAdmin } from "@/lib/supabaseServer";

// disable next default body parser
export const runtime = "nodejs";
export const revalidate = 0;
export const config = { api: { bodyParser: false } };

export async function POST(req: NextRequest) {
  // parse multipart
  const form = new formidable.IncomingForm({ keepExtensions: true });
  const parsed = await new Promise<{ file: formidable.File }>((resolve, reject) => {
    form.parse(req as any, (err, fields, files) => {
      if (err) reject(err);
      else resolve({ file: files.file });
    });
  });

  const file = parsed.file;
  if (!file) return NextResponse.json({ error: "no file" }, { status: 400 });

  // Read file buffer
  const buffer = fs.readFileSync(file.filepath);

  // upload to supabase storage
  const filename = `${Date.now()}_${path.basename(file.originalFilename || file.newFilename)}`;
  const bucket = "uploads";
  const { data: uploadData, error: uploadErr } = await supabaseAdmin.storage.from(bucket).upload(filename, buffer, {
    contentType: file.mimetype || undefined,
    upsert: false,
  });

  if (uploadErr) {
    console.error("uploadErr", uploadErr);
    return NextResponse.json({ error: uploadErr.message }, { status: 500 });
  }

  const { data: publicData } = supabaseAdmin.storage.from(bucket).getPublicUrl(uploadData.path);

  let extractedText: string | null = null;
  // do lightweight extraction for pdf and docx
  const lower = (file.originalFilename || "").toLowerCase();
  try {
    if (lower.endsWith(".pdf")) {
      const parsedPdf = await pdf(buffer);
      extractedText = parsedPdf.text;
    } else if (lower.endsWith(".docx")) {
      const result = await mammoth.extractRawText({ buffer });
      extractedText = result.value;
    } else {
      // other types: return only public url (PPTX/doc non-docx not extracted here)
    }
  } catch (err) {
    console.error("extraction error", err);
  }

  return NextResponse.json({
    publicUrl: publicData.publicUrl,
    extractedText,
  });
}

// app/api/ai/summarize/route.ts
import { NextRequest, NextResponse } from "next/server";

export const runtime = "edge"; // or "nodejs" if you prefer

export async function POST(req: NextRequest) {
  const { text, mode } = await req.json();

  if (!text || !mode) {
    return NextResponse.json({ error: "Missing text or mode" }, { status: 400 });
  }

  // Construct prompt for AI
  const prompt =
    mode === "improve"
      ? `Improve the following text for clarity, grammar, and style. Output only the improved text.\n\n${text}`
      : `Summarize the following text into a concise paragraph or 5 bullet points. Output only the summary.\n\n${text}`;

  const openaiKey = process.env.OPENAI_API_KEY;
  if (!openaiKey) return NextResponse.json({ error: "Missing OPENAI_API_KEY" }, { status: 500 });

  try {
    const response = await fetch("https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions", {
      method: "POST",
      headers: {
        Authorization: `Bearer ${openaiKey}`,
        "Content-Type": "application/json",
      },
      body: JSON.stringify({
        model: "gpt-4o-mini", // or gpt-4, gpt-4o if you have access
        messages: [{ role: "user", content: prompt }],
        max_tokens: 600,
        temperature: 0.2,
      }),
    });

    if (!response.ok) {
      const text = await response.text();
      console.error("OpenAI API error:", text);
      return NextResponse.json({ error: "OpenAI API error" }, { status: 500 });
    }

    const data = await response.json();
    const output = data.choices?.[0]?.message?.content || data.choices?.[0]?.text || "No output";

    return NextResponse.json({ output });
  } catch (err) {
    console.error("AI service error:", err);
    return NextResponse.json({ error: "AI service error" }, { status: 500 });
  }
}

> **The Ultimate AI-Powered Note-Taking Application** — Combine the power of rich text editing, real-time AI assistance, and secure cloud storage in one beautiful, intuitive platform.

![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-14.2-black?style=flat-square&logo=next.js)
![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-19-61DAFB?style=flat-square&logo=react)
![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-5-3178C6?style=flat-square&logo=typescript)

![Supabase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Supabase-Auth%20%26%20DB-3ECF8E?style=flat-square&logo=supabase)
![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-green?style=flat-square)

---

## 🎯 Overview

NoteForge-AI is a **modern, full-stack note-taking application** that empowers users to create, organize, and enhance their notes with real-time AI assistance. Built with cutting-edge technologies, it delivers a seamless experience for productivity and knowledge management.

### Why NoteForge-AI?

✅ **Rich Text Editing** — Professional-grade editor with formatting, tables, images, and more  
✅ **AI-Powered Intelligence** — Summarize and improve your notes with OpenAI  
✅ **Secure Authentication** — User accounts with Supabase Auth  
✅ **Cloud Storage** — All notes backed by PostgreSQL  
✅ **Dark Mode** — Beautiful light/dark theme with persistent preferences  
✅ **Responsive Design** — Works flawlessly on desktop, tablet, and mobile  
✅ **SSR-Safe** — Next.js App Router with proper hydration handling  

---

## 🚀 Key Features

### 📝 Advanced Rich Text Editor
- **TipTap-powered** editing with StarterKit extensions
- **Formatting**: Bold, italic, underline, headings, bullet lists, numbered lists
- **Tables**: Insert and manage complex table layouts
- **Images**: Upload and embed images directly into notes
- **Markdown Mode Toggle**: Switch between visual and markdown editing
- **Text Styling**: Font family picker (Sans, Serif, Mono), custom font colors
- **Undo/Redo**: Full edit history support

### 🧠 AI-Powered Enhancements
- **Summarize**: Generate concise summaries of long notes using OpenAI
- **Improve**: Get AI suggestions to enhance clarity and quality
- **Real-time Processing**: Debounced AI calls for smooth performance
- **Smart Content Generation**: Charts, graphs, and visual data representation

### 📊 Data Visualization
- **Chart Insertion**: Create line, bar, and pie charts directly in notes
- **SVG-based Rendering**: Lightweight, scalable charts
- **PPT Support**: Import slides from PowerPoint presentations
- **File Imports**: Extract text from PDF and DOCX documents

### 🔐 Security & Authentication
- **Supabase Auth**: Secure login/signup with email
- **Session Management**: Automatic user persistence
- **Protected Routes**: Dashboard and editor accessible only to authenticated users
- **Database-backed Notes**: All data encrypted and stored in PostgreSQL

### 🎨 User Experience
- **Dark/Light Mode**: Toggle theme with localStorage persistence
- **Responsive Grid Layout**: Optimized sidebar + editor layout
- **Loading States**: Visual feedback for saves, uploads, and AI processing
- **Error Handling**: User-friendly error messages and alerts

---

## 🛠️ Tech Stack

| Layer | Technology | Purpose |
|-------|-----------|---------|
| **Frontend** | Next.js 14.2 (App Router) | Server-rendered React app |
| **Styling** | Tailwind CSS 4 + classnames | Responsive, dark-mode-ready UI |
| **Editor** | TipTap 3.13 | Rich text editing with extensions |
| **Database** | Supabase (PostgreSQL) | Note storage & user data |
| **Auth** | Supabase Auth | Secure user authentication |
| **AI** | OpenAI API (GPT-4o Mini) | Text summarization & improvement |
| **Language** | TypeScript 5 | Type-safe development |
| **Form Handling** | Native FormData API | File uploads & API calls |

### Core Dependencies
```json
{
  "@tiptap/react": "^3.13.0",
  "@tiptap/starter-kit": "Latest",
  "@tiptap/extension-*": "Color, TextStyle, Image, Link, Table, Underline",
  "@supabase/supabase-js": "^2.x",
  "next": "^14.2.33",
  "react": "^19.0.0",
  "tailwindcss": "^4.0.0"
}
```

---

## 📦 Installation & Setup

### Prerequisites
- **Node.js** 18+ and npm
- **Git** for version control
- **Supabase Account** (free tier available at [supabase.com](https://supabase.com))
- **OpenAI API Key** (for AI features)

### 1. Clone the Repository

```bash
git clone https://github.com/siddharth-roy27/NoteForge-AI.git
cd NoteForge-AI
```

### 2. Install Dependencies

```bash
npm install
```

Or with Yarn/PNPM:
```bash
yarn install
# or
pnpm install
```

### 3. Environment Setup

Create a `.env.local` file in the root directory:

```env
# Supabase
NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL=https://your-project.supabase.co
NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY=your-anon-key

# OpenAI (for AI features)
OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-your-api-key-here
```

**How to get these values:**
1. **Supabase URL & Anon Key**: Visit [Supabase Dashboard](https://app.supabase.com) → Project Settings → API
2. **OpenAI API Key**: Create account at [openai.com](https://openai.com) and generate API keys

### 4. Database Setup (Supabase)

Create a `notes` table in Supabase:

```sql
CREATE TABLE notes (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  user_id UUID REFERENCES auth.users ON DELETE CASCADE,
  title TEXT,
  content TEXT,
  created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT NOW(),
  updated_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT NOW()
);

CREATE INDEX ON notes(user_id);
```

### 5. Run Development Server

```bash
npm run dev
```

Open **http://localhost:3000** in your browser.

### 6. Build for Production

```bash
npm run build
npm start
```

---

```
noteforge-ai/
├── app/
│   ├── api/                      # API routes
│   │   ├── ai/summarize/         # OpenAI text processing
│   │   ├── auth/                 # Login, signup, logout endpoints
│   │   ├── notes/                # CRUD operations for notes
│   │   └── upload/               # File upload handler
│   ├── auth/                     # Authentication pages (login/signup)
│   ├── dashboard/                # Main note editor interface
│   │   └── components/
│   │       ├── Editor.tsx        # Rich text editor (TipTap)
│   │       └── NoteCard.tsx      # Note preview card
│   ├── globals.css               # Global styles + Tailwind
│   ├── layout.tsx                # Root layout with theme
│   └── page.tsx                  # Landing page
├── components/
│   └── Navbar.tsx                # Navigation + theme toggle
├── lib/
│   └── supabase.ts               # Supabase client initialization
├── public/                       # Static assets
├── package.json                  # Dependencies & scripts
├── tsconfig.json                 # TypeScript configuration
└── tailwind.config.ts            # Tailwind CSS configuration
```

## 🎮 Usage Guide

### Creating a Note
1. Click **"New Note"** in the dashboard
2. Enter a title
3. Start typing or paste content
4. Click **"Save"** to store

### Using AI Features
- **Summarize**: Select text → Click "Summarize" button
- **Improve**: Select text → Click "Improve" for AI enhancement
- Auto-save with debounced AI calls every 2 seconds

### Formatting
- Use toolbar buttons for **bold**, *italic*, <u>underline</u>
- Insert **headings** (H1, H2, H3)
- Create **lists** (bullet or numbered)
- Add **tables** with customizable rows/columns

### Advanced Features
- 🎨 **Font Picker**: Change font family (Sans, Serif, Mono)
- 🎨 **Color Picker**: Apply custom text colors
- 📊 **Chart Insertion**: Generate line, bar, or pie charts
- 📥 **File Import**: Upload PDF, DOCX, or PPTX
- 🌙 **Theme Toggle**: Switch dark/light mode (saved to localStorage)

---

## 🔧 Configuration

### Tailwind CSS
Customize styles in `tailwind.config.ts`:
```ts
export default {
  theme: {
    extend: {
      colors: {
        // Add custom colors
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### TipTap Extensions
Modify editor capabilities in `app/dashboard/components/Editor.tsx`:
```tsx
const editor = useEditor({
  extensions: [
    StarterKit,
    // Add more extensions here
  ]
})
```

---

## 🚨 Troubleshooting

### "Module not found: '@/lib/supabase'"
- Ensure `tsconfig.json` has correct path mappings
- Rebuild with `npm run build`

### "SSR Hydration Mismatch"
- Editor uses `immediatelyRender: false` and mounted state check
- Navbar wraps interactive elements in `mounted` guard
- This is expected and handled correctly

### "OpenAI API Error"
- Verify `OPENAI_API_KEY` in `.env.local`
- Check API key permissions and billing status

### "Supabase Connection Failed"
- Confirm `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` and `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`
- Network connectivity and Supabase service status

---

## 🔐 Security Best Practices

✅ **Environment Variables**: Never commit `.env.local` to Git  
✅ **API Keys**: Use server-side routes for sensitive operations  
✅ **Database**: Row-level security (RLS) enforced on Supabase  
✅ **Authentication**: Session tokens managed by Supabase Auth  
✅ **HTTPS**: Always use HTTPS in production  

---

## 📊 Performance Optimizations

- **Server-Side Rendering (SSR)**: Next.js App Router for fast initial loads
- **Debounced AI Calls**: Reduces API calls while user is typing
- **Image Optimization**: Next.js `Image` component for lazy loading
- **CSS-in-JS**: Tailwind for minimal bundle size
- **Code Splitting**: Dynamic imports for heavy components

NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL=https://your-project.supabase.co
NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY=your-anon-key

# OpenAI (for AI features)
OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-your-api-key-here
```

**How to get these values:**
1. **Supabase URL & Anon Key**: Visit [Supabase Dashboard](https://app.supabase.com) → Project Settings → API
2. **OpenAI API Key**: Create account at [openai.com](https://openai.com) and generate API keys

### 4. Database Setup (Supabase)

Create a `notes` table in Supabase:

```sql
CREATE TABLE notes (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  user_id UUID REFERENCES auth.users ON DELETE CASCADE,
  title TEXT,
  content TEXT,
  created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT NOW(),
  updated_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT NOW()
);

CREATE INDEX ON notes(user_id);
```

### 5. Run Development Server

```bash
npm run dev
```

Open **http://localhost:3000** in your browser.

### 6. Build for Production

```bash
npm run build
npm start
```

## 🎮 Usage Guide

### Creating a Note
1. Click **"New Note"** in the dashboard
2. Enter a title
3. Start typing or paste content
4. Click **"Save"** to store

### Using AI Features
- **Summarize**: Select text → Click "Summarize" button
- **Improve**: Select text → Click "Improve" for AI enhancement
- Auto-save with debounced AI calls every 2 seconds

### Formatting
- Use toolbar buttons for **bold**, *italic*, <u>underline</u>
- Insert **headings** (H1, H2, H3)
- Create **lists** (bullet or numbered)
- Add **tables** with customizable rows/columns

### Advanced Features
- 🎨 **Font Picker**: Change font family (Sans, Serif, Mono)
- 🎨 **Color Picker**: Apply custom text colors
- 📊 **Chart Insertion**: Generate line, bar, or pie charts
- 📥 **File Import**: Upload PDF, DOCX, or PPTX
- 🌙 **Theme Toggle**: Switch dark/light mode (saved to localStorage)

---

## 🔧 Configuration

### Tailwind CSS
Customize styles in `tailwind.config.ts`:
```ts
export default {
  theme: {
    extend: {
      colors: {
        // Add custom colors
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### TipTap Extensions
Modify editor capabilities in `app/dashboard/components/Editor.tsx`:
```tsx
const editor = useEditor({
  extensions: [
    StarterKit,
    // Add more extensions here
  ]
})
```

---

## 🚨 Troubleshooting

### "Module not found: '@/lib/supabase'"
- Ensure `tsconfig.json` has correct path mappings
- Rebuild with `npm run build`

### "SSR Hydration Mismatch"
- Editor uses `immediatelyRender: false` and mounted state check
- Navbar wraps interactive elements in `mounted` guard
- This is expected and handled correctly

### "OpenAI API Error"
- Verify `OPENAI_API_KEY` in `.env.local`
- Check API key permissions and billing status

### "Supabase Connection Failed"
- Confirm `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` and `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`
- Network connectivity and Supabase service status

---

## 🔐 Security Best Practices

✅ **Environment Variables**: Never commit `.env.local` to Git  
✅ **API Keys**: Use server-side routes for sensitive operations  
✅ **Database**: Row-level security (RLS) enforced on Supabase  
✅ **Authentication**: Session tokens managed by Supabase Auth  
✅ **HTTPS**: Always use HTTPS in production  

---

## 📊 Performance Optimizations

- **Server-Side Rendering (SSR)**: Next.js App Router for fast initial loads
- **Debounced AI Calls**: Reduces API calls while user is typing
- **Image Optimization**: Next.js `Image` component for lazy loading
- **CSS-in-JS**: Tailwind for minimal bundle size
- **Code Splitting**: Dynamic imports for heavy components

### 3. Environment Setup

Create a `.env.local` file in the root directory with all required keys:

```env
# ============================================
# PUBLIC KEYS (Client-side, safe to expose)
# ============================================
NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL=https://your-project.supabase.co
NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY=your-anon-key

# ============================================
# SECRET KEYS (Server-side only)
# ============================================
OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-your-api-key-here
STRIPE_SECRET_KEY=sk_live_your-stripe-secret-key

# ============================================
# PUBLIC STRIPE KEYS (Client-side)
# ============================================
NEXT_PUBLIC_STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY=pk_live_your-stripe-publishable-key
```

#### 📌 Key Classification

| Environment Variable | Type | Location | Visibility | Purpose |
|---------------------|------|----------|-----------|---------|
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` | Public | `.env.local` | Client-side safe | Supabase project URL |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` | Public | `.env.local` | Client-side safe | Supabase anonymous key (for browser) |
| `OPENAI_API_KEY` | Secret | `.env.local` | Server-side only | OpenAI API calls (kept on server) |

{"content": "# 📋 Environment Variables Guide

## Overview

NoteForge-AI uses two environment files with clear separation of concerns:

- **`.env`** → Server-side secrets (NEVER commit, use in production CI/CD)
- **`.env.local`** → Local development (includes both public & secret keys)

---

## 🔓 PUBLIC Keys (Safe to Expose)

These keys are prefixed with `NEXT_PUBLIC_` and are accessible from the browser:

| Key | File | Purpose | Where Used |
|-----|------|---------|-----------|
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` | `.env.local` | Supabase project URL | Client-side (browser) |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` | `.env.local` | Supabase anonymous key | Client-side (browser) |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` | `.env.local` | Stripe payment forms | Client-side (browser) |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` | `.env.local` | Google OAuth login | Client-side (browser) |

**✅ Safe to commit** (won't be blocked by GitHub)

---

## 🔐 SECRET Keys (NEVER Expose to Client)

These keys should ONLY be used on the server-side and NEVER accessed from the browser:

### `.env.local` (Local Development)

| Key | Purpose | Where Used | Visibility |
|-----|---------|-----------|-----------|
| `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` | Admin operations on Supabase | Server-side routes only | 🔐 Secret |
| `DATABASE_URL` | Direct PostgreSQL connection | Server-side routes only | 🔐 Secret |
| `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` | Process payments, refunds | Server-side routes only | 🔐 Secret |
| `STRIPE_RESTRICTED_KEY` | Optional: Limited Stripe permissions | Server-side routes only | 🔐 Secret |
| `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` | Verify Stripe webhook events | Server-side routes only | 🔐 Secret |
| `OPENAI_API_KEY` | Call OpenAI API | Server-side routes only | 🔐 Secret |
| `GEMINI_API_KEY` | Call Google Gemini API | Server-side routes only | 🔐 Secret |
| `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET` | Google OAuth backend | Server-side routes only | 🔐 Secret |
| `NEXTAUTH_SECRET` | NextAuth session signing | Server-side routes only | 🔐 Secret |

**❌ NEVER commit** (GitHub will block it)

### `.env` (Production/CI-CD Only)

Contains the same secret keys as `.env.local` but:
- Used in production environments
- Added to CI/CD secrets (GitHub, Vercel, etc.)
- NEVER committed to Git

---

## 📌 Stripe Keys Explained

Stripe provides **3 types of keys**:

### 1. **Publishable Key** (`pk_test_...` or `pk_live_...`)
- ✅ **Safe to expose publicly**
- Used in **client-side code**
- Front-end payment forms and Stripe.js
- Prefixed with `NEXT_PUBLIC_STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY`

```jsx
// ✅ CLIENT-SIDE (Safe in browser)
const stripe = loadStripe(process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY);
```

### 2. **Secret Key** (`sk_test_...` or `sk_live_...`)
- 🔐 **KEEP SECRET — NEVER expose to client**
- Used in **server-side routes only**
- Process payments, refunds, customer management
- Full API permissions

```js
// ✅ SERVER-SIDE ONLY (API route, never in browser)
// app/api/stripe/create-checkout/route.ts
const stripe = new Stripe(process.env.STRIPE_SECRET_KEY);
```

### 3. **Restricted API Key** (`rk_test_...` or `rk_live_...`)
- 🔐 **KEEP SECRET — Optional alternative**
- More limited permissions than full Secret Key
- Enhanced security (only what you need)
- Use if you want finer control

```js
// ✅ SERVER-SIDE ONLY (Alternative to Secret Key)
const stripe = new Stripe(process.env.STRIPE_RESTRICTED_KEY);
```

---

## 📝 Key Placement Reference

### `.env.local` (Local Development)

```env
# ✅ PUBLIC (Client-side safe)
NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL="https://..."
NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY="eyJ..."
NEXT_PUBLIC_STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY="pk_test_..."
NEXT_PUBLIC_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID="957729..."

# 🔐 SECRET (Server-side only)
SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY="eyJ..."
DATABASE_URL="postgresql://..."
STRIPE_SECRET_KEY="sk_test_..."
STRIPE_RESTRICTED_KEY="rk_test_..."
STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET="whsec_..."
OPENAI_API_KEY="sk-proj-..."
GEMINI_API_KEY="AIzaSy..."
GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET="GOCSPX..."
NEXTAUTH_SECRET="aTB2kR9p..."
NEXTAUTH_URL="http://localhost:3000"
NODE_ENV="development"
```

### `.env` (Production)

```env
# Same secret keys as .env.local
DATABASE_URL="postgresql://..."
SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY="eyJ..."
STRIPE_SECRET_KEY="sk_live_..."
OPENAI_API_KEY="sk-proj-..."
GEMINI_API_KEY="AIzaSy..."
GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET="GOCSPX..."
NEXTAUTH_SECRET="<RANDOM_SECRET>"
NEXTAUTH_URL="https://yourdomain.com"
```

---

## 🚀 Setup Checklist

- [ ] Create `.env.local` with all keys
- [ ] Create `.env` with secret keys (for production/CI-CD)
- [ ] Add `.env.local` to `.gitignore`
- [ ] Add `.env` to `.gitignore` (if in monorepo, or handle with CI/CD secrets)
- [ ] Verify `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` keys are safe to expose
- [ ] Verify secret keys are server-side only (not in client code)
- [ ] Test that browser doesn't have access to secret keys

---

## ⚠️ Security Best Practices

1. **Never commit `.env.local`** or `.env` to Git
2. **Never log secret keys** (use `console.log()` to verify they exist)
3. **Use environment-specific keys** (test keys in dev, live keys in production)
4. **Rotate keys regularly** (especially after security incidents)
5. **Use GitHub Secrets** for CI/CD (Actions, Vercel, Netlify, etc.)
6. **Lock down API permissions** (Stripe Restricted Key, Supabase RLS, etc.)

---

## 🔧 How to Generate Missing Keys

### OpenAI API Key
1. Visit https://platform.openai.com/api-keys
2. Create new secret key
3. Copy to `.env.local` as `OPENAI_API_KEY`

### Supabase Keys
1. Go to https://app.supabase.com
2. Select your project
3. Settings → API → Copy URL and Anon Key
4. Service Role Key is under API → Service Role (Secret)

### Stripe Keys
1. Go to https://dashboard.stripe.com
2. Developers → API Keys
3. Copy Publishable Key → `NEXT_PUBLIC_STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY`
4. Copy Secret Key → `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY`
5. Webhooks → Create endpoint → Copy Signing Secret → `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`

### Google OAuth
1. Go to https://console.cloud.google.com
2. Create OAuth 2.0 Client ID
3. Copy Client ID → `NEXT_PUBLIC_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`
4. Copy Client Secret → `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET`

### NextAuth Secret
```bash
openssl rand -base64 32
```
Copy output to `NEXTAUTH_SECRET`

---

> **The Ultimate AI-Powered Note-Taking Application** — Combine the power of rich text editing, real-time AI assistance, and secure cloud storage in one beautiful, intuitive platform.

![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-green?style=flat-square)

---

##  Overview

NoteForge-AI is a **modern, full-stack note-taking application** that empowers users to create, organize, and enhance their notes with real-time AI assistance. Built with cutting-edge technologies, it delivers a seamless experience for productivity and knowledge management.

### Why NoteForge-AI?

 **Rich Text Editing** — Professional-grade editor with formatting, tables, images, and more  
 **AI-Powered Intelligence** — Summarize and improve your notes with OpenAI  
 **Secure Authentication** — User accounts with Supabase Auth  
 **Cloud Storage** — All notes backed by PostgreSQL  
 **Dark Mode** — Beautiful light/dark theme with persistent preferences  
 **Responsive Design** — Works flawlessly on desktop, tablet, and mobile  
 **SSR-Safe** — Next.js App Router with proper hydration handling  

---

##  Key Features

### 📝 Advanced Rich Text Editor
- **TipTap-powered** editing with StarterKit extensions
- **Formatting**: Bold, italic, underline, headings, bullet lists, numbered lists
- **Tables**: Insert and manage complex table layouts
- **Images**: Upload and embed images directly into notes
- **Markdown Mode Toggle**: Switch between visual and markdown editing
- **Text Styling**: Font family picker (Sans, Serif, Mono), custom font colors
- **Undo/Redo**: Full edit history support

### 🧠 AI-Powered Enhancements
- **Summarize**: Generate concise summaries of long notes using OpenAI
- **Improve**: Get AI suggestions to enhance clarity and quality
- **Real-time Processing**: Debounced AI calls for smooth performance
- **Smart Content Generation**: Charts, graphs, and visual data representation

### 📊 Data Visualization
- **Chart Insertion**: Create line, bar, and pie charts directly in notes
- **SVG-based Rendering**: Lightweight, scalable charts
- **PPT Support**: Import slides from PowerPoint presentations
- **File Imports**: Extract text from PDF and DOCX documents

### 🔐 Security & Authentication
- **Supabase Auth**: Secure login/signup with email
- **Session Management**: Automatic user persistence
- **Protected Routes**: Dashboard and editor accessible only to authenticated users
- **Database-backed Notes**: All data encrypted and stored in PostgreSQL

### 🎨 User Experience
- **Dark/Light Mode**: Toggle theme with localStorage persistence
- **Responsive Grid Layout**: Optimized sidebar + editor layout
- **Loading States**: Visual feedback for saves, uploads, and AI processing
- **Error Handling**: User-friendly error messages and alerts

---

## 🛠️ Tech Stack

| Layer | Technology | Purpose |
|-------|-----------|---------|
| **Frontend** | Next.js 14.2 (App Router) | Server-rendered React app |
| **Styling** | Tailwind CSS 4 + classnames | Responsive, dark-mode-ready UI |
| **Editor** | TipTap 3.13 | Rich text editing with extensions |
| **Database** | Supabase (PostgreSQL) | Note storage & user data |
| **Auth** | Supabase Auth | Secure user authentication |
| **AI** | OpenAI API (GPT-4o Mini) | Text summarization & improvement |
| **Language** | TypeScript 5 | Type-safe development |
| **Form Handling** | Native FormData API | File uploads & API calls |

### Core Dependencies

{
  "@tiptap/react": "^3.13.0",
  "@tiptap/starter-kit": "Latest",
  "@tiptap/extension-*": "Color, TextStyle, Image, Link, Table, Underline",
  "@supabase/supabase-js": "^2.x",
  "next": "^14.2.33",
  "react": "^19.0.0",
  "tailwindcss": "^4.0.0"
}
```

---

## 📦 Installation & Setup

### Prerequisites
- **Node.js** 18+ and npm
- **Git** for version control
- **Supabase Account** (free tier available at [supabase.com](https://supabase.com))
- **OpenAI API Key** (for AI features)

### 1. Clone the Repository

```bash
git clone https://github.com/siddharth-roy27/NoteForge-AI.git
cd NoteForge-AI
```

### 2. Install Dependencies

```bash
npm install
```

Or with Yarn/PNPM:
```bash
yarn install
# or
pnpm install
```

### 3. Environment Setup

Create a `.env.local` file in the root directory:

```env
# Supabase
NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL=https://your-project.supabase.co
NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY=your-anon-key

# Gemini (for AI features)
GEMINI_API_KEY=your-gemini-api-key-here
```

**How to get these values:**
1. **Supabase URL & Anon Key**: Visit [Supabase Dashboard](https://app.supabase.com) → Project Settings → API
2. **Gemini API Key**: Create account / enable Generative AI API in Google Cloud and generate an API key

### 4. Database Setup (Supabase)

Create a `notes` table in Supabase:

```sql

# 📋 Environment Variables Guide

## Overview

NoteForge-AI uses two environment files with clear separation of concerns:

- **`.env`** → Server-side secrets (NEVER commit, use in production CI/CD)
- **`.env.local`** → Local development (includes both public & secret keys)

---

## 🔓 PUBLIC Keys (Safe to Expose)

These keys are prefixed with `NEXT_PUBLIC_` and are accessible from the browser:

| Key | File | Purpose | Where Used |
|-----|------|---------|-----------|
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` | `.env.local` | Supabase project URL | Client-side (browser) |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` | `.env.local` | Supabase anonymous key | Client-side (browser) |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` | `.env.local` | Stripe payment forms | Client-side (browser) |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` | `.env.local` | Google OAuth login | Client-side (browser) |

**✅ Safe to commit** (won't be blocked by GitHub)

---

## 🔐 SECRET Keys (NEVER Expose to Client)

These keys should ONLY be used on the server-side and NEVER accessed from the browser:

### `.env.local` (Local Development)

| Key | Purpose | Where Used | Visibility |
|-----|---------|-----------|-----------|
| `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` | Admin operations on Supabase | Server-side routes only | 🔐 Secret |
| `DATABASE_URL` | Direct PostgreSQL connection | Server-side routes only | 🔐 Secret |
| `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` | Process payments, refunds | Server-side routes only | 🔐 Secret |
| `STRIPE_RESTRICTED_KEY` | Optional: Limited Stripe permissions | Server-side routes only | 🔐 Secret |
| `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` | Verify Stripe webhook events | Server-side routes only | 🔐 Secret |
| `GEMINI_API_KEY` | Call Google Gemini API | Server-side routes only | 🔐 Secret |
| `GEMINI_API_KEY` | Call Google Gemini API | Server-side routes only | 🔐 Secret |
| `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET` | Google OAuth backend | Server-side routes only | 🔐 Secret |
| `NEXTAUTH_SECRET` | NextAuth session signing | Server-side routes only | 🔐 Secret |

**❌ NEVER commit** (GitHub will block it)

### `.env` (Production/CI-CD Only)

Contains the same secret keys as `.env.local` but:
- Used in production environments
- Added to CI/CD secrets (GitHub, Vercel, etc.)
- NEVER committed to Git

---

## 📌 Stripe Keys Explained

Stripe provides **3 types of keys**:

### 1. **Publishable Key** (`pk_test_...` or `pk_live_...`)
- ✅ **Safe to expose publicly**
- Used in **client-side code**
- Front-end payment forms and Stripe.js
- Prefixed with `NEXT_PUBLIC_STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY`

```jsx
// ✅ CLIENT-SIDE (Safe in browser)
const stripe = loadStripe(process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY);
```

### 2. **Secret Key** (`sk_test_...` or `sk_live_...`)
- 🔐 **KEEP SECRET — NEVER expose to client**
- Used in **server-side routes only**
- Process payments, refunds, customer management
- Full API permissions

```js
// ✅ SERVER-SIDE ONLY (API route, never in browser)
// app/api/stripe/create-checkout/route.ts
const stripe = new Stripe(process.env.STRIPE_SECRET_KEY);
```

### 3. **Restricted API Key** (`rk_test_...` or `rk_live_...`)
- 🔐 **KEEP SECRET — Optional alternative**
- More limited permissions than full Secret Key
- Enhanced security (only what you need)
- Use if you want finer control

```js
// ✅ SERVER-SIDE ONLY (Alternative to Secret Key)
const stripe = new Stripe(process.env.STRIPE_RESTRICTED_KEY);
```

---

## 📝 Key Placement Reference

### `.env.local` (Local Development)

```env
# ✅ PUBLIC (Client-side safe)
NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL="https://..."
NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY="eyJ..."
NEXT_PUBLIC_STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY="pk_test_..."
NEXT_PUBLIC_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID="957729..."

# 🔐 SECRET (Server-side only)
SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY="eyJ..."
DATABASE_URL="postgresql://..."
STRIPE_SECRET_KEY="sk_test_..."
STRIPE_RESTRICTED_KEY="rk_test_..."
STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET="whsec_..."
GEMINI_API_KEY="sk-proj-..."
GEMINI_API_KEY="AIzaSy..."
GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET="GOCSPX..."
NEXTAUTH_SECRET="aTB2kR9p..."
NEXTAUTH_URL="http://localhost:3000"
NODE_ENV="development"
```

### `.env` (Production)

```env
# Same secret keys as .env.local
DATABASE_URL="postgresql://..."
SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY="eyJ..."
STRIPE_SECRET_KEY="sk_live_..."
GEMINI_API_KEY="sk-proj-..."
GEMINI_API_KEY="AIzaSy..."
GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET="GOCSPX..."
NEXTAUTH_SECRET="<RANDOM_SECRET>"
NEXTAUTH_URL="https://yourdomain.com"
```

---

## 🚀 Setup Checklist

- [ ] Create `.env.local` with all keys
- [ ] Create `.env` with secret keys (for production/CI-CD)
- [ ] Add `.env.local` to `.gitignore`
- [ ] Add `.env` to `.gitignore` (if in monorepo, or handle with CI/CD secrets)
- [ ] Verify `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` keys are safe to expose
- [ ] Verify secret keys are server-side only (not in client code)
- [ ] Test that browser doesn't have access to secret keys

---

## ⚠️ Security Best Practices

1. **Never commit `.env.local`** or `.env` to Git
2. **Never log secret keys** (use `console.log()` to verify they exist)
3. **Use environment-specific keys** (test keys in dev, live keys in production)
4. **Rotate keys regularly** (especially after security incidents)
5. **Use GitHub Secrets** for CI/CD (Actions, Vercel, Netlify, etc.)
6. **Lock down API permissions** (Stripe Restricted Key, Supabase RLS, etc.)

---

## 🔧 How to Generate Missing Keys

### Gemini (Google) API Key
1. Visit https://console.cloud.google.com/apis & enable the Generative AI (Gemini) API for your project
2. Create an API key under **APIs & Services → Credentials**
3. Copy to `.env.local` as `GEMINI_API_KEY`

### Supabase Keys
1. Go to https://app.supabase.com
2. Select your project
3. Settings → API → Copy URL and Anon Key
4. Service Role Key is under API → Service Role (Secret)

### Stripe Keys
1. Go to https://dashboard.stripe.com
2. Developers → API Keys
3. Copy Publishable Key → `NEXT_PUBLIC_STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY`
4. Copy Secret Key → `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY`
5. Webhooks → Create endpoint → Copy Signing Secret → `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`

### Google OAuth
1. Go to https://console.cloud.google.com
2. Create OAuth 2.0 Client ID
3. Copy Client ID → `NEXT_PUBLIC_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`
4. Copy Client Secret → `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET`

### NextAuth Secret
```bash
openssl rand -base64 32
```
Copy output to `NEXTAUTH_SECRET`

---

# NoteForge AI - Complete Setup Instructions

## 🚀 Quick Setup

### 1. Install Dependencies
```bash
npm install
```

### 2. Set Up Environment Variables
```bash
# Copy the example file
cp .env.local.example .env.local

# Edit `.env.local` with your actual values. Do NOT commit this file.
```

Notes:
- Keep secrets (API keys, Stripe secret, NEXTAUTH_SECRET) only in `.env.local` or your host's secret manager.
- The project now uses Google Gemini for AI features. Provide `GEMINI_API_KEY` (server side).

### 3. Set Up Supabase Database

1. Go to your Supabase project: https://supabase.com/dashboard
2. Navigate to **SQL Editor**
3. Copy the contents of `supabase/migrations/001_initial_schema.sql`
4. Paste and run it in the SQL Editor
5. This will create all tables, RLS policies, and triggers

### 4. Set Up Supabase Storage

1. In Supabase Dashboard, go to **Storage**
2. The SQL migration should have created the `note-attachments` bucket
3. If not, create it manually:
   - Name: `note-attachments`
   - Public: `true`

1. In Stripe Dashboard, go to **Developers > Webhooks**

3. Select events:
   - `checkout.session.completed`
   - `customer.subscription.updated`
   - `customer.subscription.deleted`
4. Copy the **Signing secret** to `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` in `.env.local`

### 6. Run the Development Server
```bash
npm run dev
```

## 🔧 Troubleshooting

### Error: "Failed to create note"
**Cause:** Database tables don't exist or RLS policies not set up

**Fix:**
1. Run the SQL migration in Supabase SQL Editor
2. Verify tables exist: `profiles`, `notes`, `folders`, `tags`, `note_tags`
3. Check RLS is enabled on all tables

### Error: "Unauthorized" or "Permission denied"
**Cause:** RLS policies not configured correctly

**Fix:**
1. Run the SQL migration (it includes all RLS policies)
2. Verify user is authenticated
3. Check Supabase Auth is working

### Error: "Missing environment variable"
**Cause:** `.env.local` not created or missing variables

**Fix:**
1. Create `.env.local` from `.env.local.example`
2. Fill in all required variables
3. Restart the dev server: `npm run dev`

### AI Features Not Working
**Cause:** API keys not set or invalid

**Fix:**
1. Ensure `GEMINI_API_KEY` is set in `.env.local` (server-side key).
2. If using Google Cloud, obtain a key from the Google Cloud Console and enable the Generative Language API.
   - Docs: https://developers.generativeai.google/
3. Verify API key is valid and has sufficient quota/permissions.
